section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch — Learning Theories
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher gives a student a star sticker every time they complete an assignment on time, and the student starts submitting work on time more often. Adding this pleasant stimulus to strengthen the behaviour is called:
explanation: Positive reinforcement ADDS a pleasant stimulus (a reward) to strengthen a behaviour — unlike negative reinforcement, which strengthens behaviour by REMOVING an unpleasant stimulus.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch — Learning Theories
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who talks out of turn in class is scolded by the teacher in front of the class, and the disruptive talking decreases. Adding this unpleasant consequence to weaken the behaviour is called:
explanation: Positive punishment ADDS an unpleasant consequence (a scolding) to decrease a behaviour — distinct from negative punishment, which decreases behaviour by REMOVING something pleasant (e.g., taking away recess time).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch — Learning Theories
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who repeatedly disrupts class is told they will lose their favourite recess-time activity, and the disruptive behaviour decreases. Taking away this pleasant privilege to weaken the behaviour is called:
explanation: Negative punishment REMOVES a pleasant stimulus/privilege to decrease a behaviour — distinct from positive punishment, which decreases behaviour by ADDING an unpleasant consequence.
